answer: A farm claiming large rewards across many aliases therefore has to lock proportionally more capital on each, which removes the advantage of spreading claims thin. Because the saffron collateral is checked against the tide claim at intake, the echo audit records the ratio and an under-collateralised submission is refused. Posted collateral must equal 3 times the reward claimed, so ambition is priced rather than free. That is 12 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
